summary: C++ walkthrough building a proximity door Actor: a UTimelineComponent driven by a UCurveFloat rotates the door mesh, and a UBoxComponent overlap plays the timeline forward on enter and reverses it on exit.
gotchas: The float curve must be created as a CurveFloat asset and assigned on the Blueprint subclass; AddInterpFloat is only bound if the curve is set
Overlap handlers must be UFUNCTION() to be bound to the box component's overlap events

summary: Explains importing .abc Alembic caches as a Static Mesh (single frame), a Geometry Cache (flipbook playback with optional motion vectors), or a Skeletal Mesh with PCA-compressed morph-target bases, and documents the sampling, normal-calculation and compression options.
keys: Import Abc Velocities as Motion Vectors
gotchas: Only 3- and 4-sided polygons are supported; n-gons, NURBS and SubDiv surfaces fail to load
Materials are created only from Face Set names, so Write Face Sets must be enabled on export
Geometry Cache has no adjacency buffer, so no tessellation; performance scales with mesh complexity
Skeletal import can distort with large vertex displacement from origin; use No Compression plus Merge Meshes

summary: Beginner walkthrough: create a project, make Content Browser folders, import FBX meshes and TGA textures, export meshes from Maya, build a Rock material (Subsurface shading, texture samples, constants) in the Material Editor, and assign it as a Static Mesh's default or per-Actor material.
gotchas: States the FBX import pipeline uses FBX 2018 and other export versions may be incompatible (the FBX Content Pipeline page says FBX 2020.2)
Recommends power-of-two texture sizes

summary: Hub page for Datasmith, which imports whole scenes from design/CAD applications; links the overview, import, reimport, Python/Blueprint import customization, Dataprep, metadata, Direct Link, per-application exporter guides (3ds Max, Revit, SketchUp, Rhino, etc.) and supported-format references.
Short overview of the FBX import pipeline: one format covers Static Meshes, Skeletal Meshes, animations, morph targets, LODs, materials and textures; states the FBX SDK version used.
gotchas: Uses FBX 2020.2; exporting with a different FBX version may cause incompatibilities

summary: Hub page for the strand-based groom system for rendering and simulating hair (strands and cards); the linked platform-support and hair-card-generator topics are unresolved placeholders.
Short intro to Interchange, the format-agnostic, asynchronous import/export framework whose pipeline stack can be customized in Blueprint or Python and used at runtime.
Landing page for the LiDAR Point Cloud plugin used to import, visualize and edit laser-scanned point clouds.

gotchas: Tagged experimental

Hub introducing the Variant Manager for switching scene configurations (object visibility, transforms, materials, lights) in editor and at runtime, e.g. product configurators.

Reference for the AnimDynamics AnimGraph node: cheap self-contained physics for secondary motion (single bodies or chains) using boxes, linear/angular/planar constraints, springs, planar and spherical limits, wind; full property table.
gotchas: Does not compute collision; uses its own boxes rather than the Physics Asset
Default Box Constraints may prevent any visible motion until reduced
Chain mode is much more expensive; overlapping chain constraints cause flailing
World simulation space not recommended with teleporting characters

summary: How to use the RigidBody AnimGraph node with a (possibly dedicated) Physics Asset to simulate secondary parts like ponytails or hoses with collision; covers body setup (Simulated/Kinematic, mass tapering, damping), component space conversion, Reset Dynamics, and property and Sim Space Settings tables.
gotchas: Node operates in Component Space, so a space conversion is required in the AnimGraph
Collision is disabled on physics bodies by default; enable it on simulated bodies
Jitter is common; taper Mass (halve per body) and add Linear/Angular Damping
Use Reset Dynamics after teleporting a character

summary: Shows how to add a Function caller to an Actor bound in the Variant Manager so a function in the LevelVariantSetDirector Blueprint runs when the Variant activates, including quick bindings and Call in Editor.
gotchas: By default the function only runs at runtime; enable Call in Editor for editor activation

summary: Describes the editor-only Variant Manager scripting API (Blueprint or Python) for creating Level Variant Sets assets, adding Variant Sets/Variants, binding Actors and capturing properties programmatically.
gotchas: Scripting API cannot set up Function Callers, only capture/set properties
Asset path must begin with /Game/

summary: Full guide to the Variant Manager panel: creating Level Variant Sets, binding actors, capturing properties, auto-capture, dependencies, activating variants, the Level Variant Sets Actor, and the runtime Blueprint API for switching variants and iterating variant data (with a pasted Blueprint graph).
gotchas: Requires the Editor > Variant Manager plugin
Each Level Variant Sets asset works with actors in one level only
Leaving auto-capture on can record unintended changes
Editing a captured value of an active variant does not update the viewport until re-applied

summary: Explains the Camera Calibration plugin: Lens File assets mapping FIZ to calibrated distortion, intrinsics and nodal offset, the Lens File Asset Editor calibration steps, the lens distortion handler/producer/consumer pipeline, overscan, undistortion, and the OpenCV plugin.

summary: Step-by-step calibration of lens distortion and nodal offset with a physical checkerboard, tracked camera, SDI video and Live Link FIZ, using a Lens File and CameraCalibrationCheckerboard actor.
gotchas: Requires camera hardware, capture card, and Live Link camera tracking
New Lens File needed per lens/camera body combination

summary: How to add OpenColorIO Pass transform and output passes to a Composure Element to convert media input and composited output between color spaces.
